Recently with the help of Claude Code, I was able to port the majority of the Autosubst2 library from Rocq to Lean https://github.com/qcfu-bu/lean-autosubst.

This library deals with the generating boilerplate code for variable substitutions (DeBruijn Indices) in programming languages. Currently, I have strong normalization of Church-style System-F formalized as a case study. Is this something that folks here are interested in?

I won't have as much bandwidth for this the next six months while I'm away for an internship, but this is something myself and others have been working on and are interested in having in CSLib. (Though I've mostly been mulling over the design, so there's nothing public from me available.).

There are two dimensions I'd like us to additionally explore however:

  • Having extensibility for adding different binding backends, like LNgen that allows locally namless binding.
  • Reifying into a representation that makes use of docs#Lean.Expr, similar to the recent work on Sulfur

So yes, I am interested as a maintainer for lambda calculus but for me a crucial component is that this ties in with the existing work we have on locally nameless binding, and in general takes note of the more recent literature to give us something even a bit nicer than a direct Autosubst port.
We've also been discussing a port of nominal sets from Rocq. I have it in CatCrypt, from nominal SSProve, but I'd like to check with the original author first.

I'm interested in that and I've been thinking about building a unified binding framework that has both locally nameless backend and autosubst backend. I haven't written any implementation code yet; I just have some early design ideas.

Interestingly I also made a locally nameless System F formalization including strongly normalization and parametricity https://github.com/berberman/systemf-ln which I'm using to draft the framework. And I guess some simple automations in my repo like applying the cofinite quantification constructor/picking fresh variables from cofintie sets might be useful in CSLib.

@Yipeng Liu We have cslib#Cslib.freeUnion for selecting fresh variables for cofinite quantification. Taking a quick look at your repo I think this is the same idea. We do have progress/preservation for System F with subtyping, (see Cslib.Languages.LambdaCalculus.LocallyNameless.Fsub.Safety) but do not have strong normalization and parametricity. PRs adding these are very welcome!
